question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(3,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(1<X<5)=0.3758,$ use the table to find  $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6808\,$ | $\,0.6844\,$ | $\,0.6879\,$ |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.7157\,$ | $\,0.7190\,$ | $\,0.7224\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7486\,$ | $\,0.7517\,$ | $\,0.7549\,$ |

*Hint: Note that the interval $1<X<5$ is symmetric about the mean $\mu =3.$*

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, note that the given interval is symmetric about the mean:

$$
P(1<X<5)=P(3-2<X<3+2)
$$

So, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X<5) & =0.3758 \\ 2P(3<X<5) & =0.3758 \\ P(3<X<5) & =0.1879 \\ P(X<5)-P(X<3) & =0.1879 \\ P(X<5)-0.5 & =0.1879 \\ P(X<5) & =0.6879 \\ P(X\le 5) & =0.6879\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5) & =0.6879 \\ P(Z\le \frac{5-3}{\sigma }) & =0.6879 \\ Φ(\frac{2}{\sigma }) & =0.6879 \\ \frac{2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.6879)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.49)=0.6879\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.6879)=0.49.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sigma } & =0.49 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{2}{0.49} \\ \sigma  & ≈4.08\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
